subject: Onprem deployment: operator custody matrix, MSA redline sprint
messages:
From: Kyle Barnes <kbarnes@medsys-ops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment redlines / operator access question

Marcus / Lauren —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of items from our side as we start internal legal review: 

- MedSys legal asks for a clear definition of "operator access" in the MSA + Order Form so we can sign off on the on‑prem deployment. Specifically: what actions entitle Redwood or an agent to access customer systems (patching, console debugging, KV export)?
- We also need an "operator custody matrix" that spells out who can hold snapshots/keys and the proposed attestation cadence. Our security team prefers a third‑party escrow option if remote operator access must be retained.
- Can Redwood provide an evidence packet (SOC 2 type artifacts + an example attestation) we can attach to our procurement file?

We'd like a proposed redline turnaround by EOD Tuesday so our legal ops can consolidate. Attaching our internal NDA excerpt for context (see attached).

Attachments: MedSys_NDA_excerpt.pdf (attachment)

Thanks,
Kyle
VP Ops — MedSys Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kyle Barnes <kbarnes@medsys-ops.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment redlines / operator access question

Kyle —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, longer below: 

1) Operator access scope: we can support three tiers — console‑view only (read), console‑limited (scoped actions: job restarts, log collection), and operator‑full (for emergency patches). We will map those to roles in the Order Form and MSA exhibit.

2) Custody & attestation: we can produce a custody matrix showing where snapshots and keys are stored, who is authorized, and the proposed quarterly attestation by an appointed Redwood security owner. We can also provide an escrow pathway via a neutral steward (third party) as an optional addendum — not the default.

3) Evidence packet: yes — SOC 2 summary, recent PCI/ISO artifacts where applicable, and an example attestation template. We'll send a zip via Drive link.

Plan: Lauren (legal) and I will run a redline sprint this week and produce an MSA + Order Form mark‑up with two paths: (A) operator access controlled with attestation, (B) operator access removed in favor of escrow custody. Can we lock Tuesday EOD as your target for receiving the initial packet?

I'll attach the MSA redline PDF and a draft operator access matrix in the follow up.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: MSA_v4_redlines.pdf, operator-access-matrix.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kyle Barnes <kbarnes@medsys-ops.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-10-10T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment redlines / operator access question

Kyle / Marcus —

Following Marcus's plan, a few legal points we will include in the redline so your counsel has clear language: 

- Definition: "Operator" will be defined as an individual authorized by Redwood to perform support activities expressly enumerated in Exhibit B (e.g., read logs, collect diagnostic snapshots, deploy hotfixes). Any activity beyond Exhibit B requires customer consent except in the case of active security incidents.
- Audit window: we propose a mutually agreed 24‑hour notification window for routine access and immediate access only for active security incidents where emergency response is required. All access must be logged and shared in the Redwood Console for 90 days (exportable CSV).
- Custody fallback: proposed clause offering two options — (i) escrow with third‑party steward and documented handover procedures, or (ii) quarterly attestation + controlled operator access with defined scope. We'll include sample redlines for both so MedSys can pick.
- Tech controls: limiting console actions by role, MFA requirement, and session recording for any operator sessions.

We'll flag the sections that will impact pricing (e.g., escrow steward costs) and call those out in the Order Form. Marcus — I'll need an internal owner for the attestation frequency and the evidence packet delivery timeline.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@medsys-legal.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kyle Barnes <kbarnes@medsys-ops.com>
Date: 2025-10-11T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment redlines / operator access question

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying notes from MedSys legal: 

- The escrow option is preferred by procurement unless Redwood can commit to a strong attestation + a 3rd party‑accessible evidence package (SOC 2, console audit exports, and the attestation reports). Please include a cost addendum for the escrow steward.
- For the attestation language, we need an explicit independence statement (Redwood security owner attesting to internal controls may not be sufficient alone).
- Can you provide a sample Docusign flow and a short description of the attestation template as a separate doc? That speeds our procurement review.

If you can send the redlines + operator matrix by EOD Tuesday, we'll try to turn comments within 48 hours. I will also loop in procurement for pricing once we have the Order Form impacts called out.

Evelyn Shaw
Sr. Counsel — MedSys Health

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/ABC-123 (shared)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2025-10-13T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Draft redlines + attachments: MSA options and custody matrix (next steps)

Evelyn / Kyle / team —

Attached are the initial deliverables per the plan: 
- MSA_v4_redlines.pdf — two tracks included: ATTTESTATION_PATH (controlled operator access + quarterly independent attestation) and ESCROW_PATH (third‑party steward custody). 
- operator-access-matrix.xlsx — granular actions mapped to roles. 
- docusign-invite.pdf — a packet showing the proposed signing flow for addenda.

Summary of next steps: 
1) Please review the MSA redlines and call out preference (Attestation vs Escrow) and any pricing flags.
2) If you prefer the escrow route, we will share a quote for the steward; if attestation, we'll loop an independent auditor (proposed: TrustWorks) and share their scope.
3) We will bake the chosen option into the Order Form and provide a final clean copy for signature.

Timeline: Redwood legal committed to an updated redline (post‑your comments) by Friday 10/17. If MedSys has procurement questions sooner, happy to set a 30‑minute alignment meeting.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
